The letter (sa) is characterized as follows:
- It is the 38th letter among the 41 letters of the Pali alphabet
- It is the 30th among the 33 consonants
- Among the six classes of sounds (kaṇṭhaja, etc.), it belongs to the dental class (dantaja)
- It is a non-grouped letter (avagga) rather than a grouped letter (vagga)
- It is the 5th letter among the 8 ungrouped consonants
- It is unvoiced (aghosa) rather than voiced (ghosa)
- Among the four tongue positions, it belongs to the middle-tongue position (jivhāmajjha)
- Among the four types of articulation (payatta), it belongs to the open articulation (vivaṭa payatta)
- Between the two types of consonants (those depending on preceding vowels and those depending on following vowels), it belongs to the parāsaya class (depending on following vowels)

The letter "s" is of three kinds -- (1) ekakkhara sa. (2) anekakkharasuddha sa which is merely "s" which is not mixed with other consonants. (3) saṃyogavanta "s" - conjunct "s" which exists together with seven consonants: t, n, m, y, r, v and s. Of them, No. (1) "s" is saṃ, sā, su and so; No. (2) "s" is of three kinds: (a) "s" at the beginning of a word, (b) "s" in the middle of a word, and (c) "s" at the end of a word. They are (a) sīla, samādhi. (b) kusala, vasabha. (c) santosa, vibhāsā, etc. No. (3) "s" is of three kinds: (a) "s" connected with the beginning consonant, (b) "s" connected with the middle consonant, and (c) "s" connected with the final consonant. They are (a) svātana, sneha, (b) vissāsa, asnāti, asmimāna, (c) Parasve, sahassa, asma, visesya, bhastra, viddhasta, etc.

The letter "sa" in the roots sā, si, sī, su, sū, se, so:
1. The root sā belongs to bhuvādi, divādi, kiyādi, gahādi groups and has meanings:
- pāka (cooking/ripening)
- antakamma (completing)
- assādana (enjoying)
- tanukara (making thin/subtle)
Forms: Verbs - sāti, sāyati, siyati, sināti, sīyati
Nouns - sāyita, sāyana, saṇha
2. The root si belongs to bhuvādi, svādi, kiyādi groups and means:
- sevā (associating)
- gati (going)
- buddhi (knowing)
- bandhana (binding)
- nisāna (sharpening)
Forms: Verbs - seti, atiseti, siṇoti, siṇāti, sināti
Nouns - sivaṃ, setu, nisita, sīmā, sīsaṃ
3. The root sī belongs to bhuvādi, kiyādi groups and means:
- sayana (sleeping)
- pāka (cooking)
Forms: Verbs - seti, sayati, siṇāti
Nouns - senaṃ, sayanaṃ, sayo, adhisayanaṃ
4. The root su belongs to bhuvādi, svādi, kiyādi groups and means:
- gati (going)
- savana (flowing/hearing)
- hiṃsā (harming)
Forms: Verbs - savati, suṇoti, suṇāti
Nouns - suto, pasuto, savanaṃ, āsavo, soto, soṇā, sāvako, parasu
5. The root sū belongs to bhuvādi, divādi groups and means:
- pāṇa (living)
- pasavana (giving birth)
Forms: Verbs - savati, pasavati, sūyati, pasūyati
Nouns - suttaṃ, pasūto, pasūtā
6. The root se belongs to bhuvādi group and means:
- khaya (destruction)
- pāka (cooking)
- gati (going)
Forms: Verbs - seti, siyati, sāyati
Nouns - setu
7. The root so belongs to divādi, gahādi groups and means:
- nisāna (sharpening)
- nāsana (destroying)
- antakamma (completing)
Forms: Verbs - siyati
Nouns - saṇha, osāna, vosāna

3. Existing, present (santa, saṃvijjamāna)

12. Successive (aparāpara)
13. Moving back and forth, wandering, repetition (saṃsaraṇa, punappuna-kiriyā)
14. Equality, harmony (sama-bhāva)

25. Well, properly (sammā, suṭṭhu)
26. All-around state (samantatta)
27. Connection (saṃyoga)
28. Strong connection (saṃyutta)
29. Relation (sambandha)
30. Turning back (parivattana)
31. Recognition (saññākaraṇa)
32. Always (nicca, nibaddha)
33. Approaching (upasaṅkamana)
34. Beginning (ādi)
35. Present moment (sampati)
36. Causing delight (paritosana)
37. Offering, supporting (pūjā, saṅgaha)
40. Facing towards (abhimukha)
41. Covering (pidhāna)
42. Completeness (samatta-bhāva)
43. Mixing (missana)
44. Knowing (maññanā)
45. Without special meaning (niratthakaṃ, pada-sobhana, padālaṅkāra)
46. Nearness (samīpa)
47. Moving, flowing (saṃsappana)
